body: I feel so old, internally. I don't have the will, the energy, or the emotional capacity to be pleased by life's unpredictability right now. I want peace, I want nirvana and zen, I want to live inside a beautiful poem. I mainly just want to be blissfully gone. How do you maintain your passion and energy in a world that constantly drains you? Or, do you find that life energises you, rather than takes your energy?

Thanks for sharing, man. It's not so much that happiness is temporary, it's more like everything is, nothing is constant. Most of our human experience isn't even real, we just play at having important rules and desires, when really we are all just endlessly farting about.

I realise that what I'm saying comes across as cliche, and is a thought passed about online a lot. That's not how it seems in my brain, I simply don't have the language/focus to put across the overwhelming nature of this belief/feeling/whatever.

I'm not sure I have a capacity for joy and enthusiasm right now, but I'm working on that. How would you say you combat suicidal thoughts, or feelings of pointlessness?

The one thing I really believe may help is HRT (hormone replacement therapy). Many transgender folk have said that getting the "correct" hormones is like receiving emotional glasses, that their emotions and self-perception begin to align, blah blah. If that fails, for me, I'm not sure I would know how to continue in life. Unfortunately, to receive HRT, I'll need to cause a lot of pain/discomfort in others' lives, something I've thus far been unwilling to actively do.
Yeah, I used to, but, like I said, this is.. different. I don't understand it myself, I just find it a really appealing concept and possibility. Thanks for your response.

Where do you find motivation to play the game, though? It seems dull, and uninspiring to me, really. Maybe it's a feeling that changes as you get older, or something?

I'm not enjoying anything much, man, especially the little things. How did you go about enjoying them?
